memory_candidates.content: When a test suite's own SUT-resolution helper is deploy-tree-first (prefers a deployed .claude/scripts/ copy over the agent-system/extensions source store), and a task edits ONLY the source store, the suite silently validates the STALE deployed copy against the new edit and reports a false green. Fix: invert resolution to source-store-first for the SUT ONLY (not its collaborator dependencies), with a comment explaining why -- precedent: test-force-phases.sh's own documented 'CANDIDATE-RESOLUTION INVERSION'. Detect this by checking which candidate path resolve_candidate() actually picked (bash -x) whenever a new assertion about freshly-edited behavior fails inexplicably.

To commit only your own hunks in a file a concurrently-dispatched sibling task is also editing: (1) git diff the file to a patch, (2) identify your hunks by @@ header line ranges vs. the sibling's (grep the diff content for markers unique to your own edit), (3) build a minimal patch (diff --git/index/---/+++ header + only your hunks) and `git apply --cached --recount --check` then apply, (4) verify with `git diff --staged` that only your hunks landed and `git diff` (unstaged) still shows the sibling's untouched hunks, (5) commit that ONE path with a manually acquired/released task-lock.sh commit-acquire/commit-release mutex and a bare `git commit -m ... -- <path>` -- NOT git-commit-scoped.sh, whose own `git add -- <path>` would re-stage the WHOLE working-tree file (including the sibling's hunks) and defeat the whole point. Commit your own exclusive files separately via the normal git-commit-scoped.sh path.

This codebase's shell files commonly carry pre-existing SC1091 (unfollowed source), SC2016 (single-quoted jq expressions with $vars), and SC2012 (ls vs find) info-level shellcheck notices that make plain `shellcheck file.sh` exit 1 even on an untouched file. When a plan says 'shellcheck clean', the practical bar is `shellcheck -S warning file.sh` exits 0 (or matches the pre-existing warning-level baseline exactly) -- diff the tool's output before vs. after your edit to confirm you introduced zero NEW warning-or-above findings, rather than chasing the info-level baseline to zero.
